analysis:
All changes are in test-only files under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/DarkbloomClusterRuntimeTests. I found no production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption, billing or cache-storage changes.

BoundedBufferCache.swift (new, lines 17-30) is a Swift Testing scoping trait. It lowers MLX's process-wide Memory.cacheLimit to min(previous, bytes) for each test, then restores the previous limit and calls Memory.clearCache() in a defer. The limit can only shrink, never grow. The helper references QwenTensorParallelLaunch.freedBufferCacheBytes and QwenDenseStageLoadPolicy.allocatorHeadroomBytes via @testable import, which are existing production symbols and are only read here.

CBv2PagedVerifyBench.swift (lines 98-118) sets and restores the cache limit in an env-gated diagnostic test. It resets Memory.peakMemory and prints peak_active_gib and cache_gib. These are numeric memory statistics only, with no prompt content, keys or identifiers.

GLM5NextTensorParallelDepthInvarianceTests.swift (lines 207 and 231) and GLM5NextTensorParallelPagedKVTests.swift (line 19) add .boundedBufferCache(gib: 4) to the synthetic-model tests.

Relation to the threat model: T-028 (residual GPU memory) and T-041 (prefix cache) concern production behavior. The trait runs only under the test harness, so it does not affect production cache limits, prefix-cache SSD storage or the TB-007 inference engine.

One residual note: the trait comment says the limit is process-wide and relies on serialization and --no-parallel in CI. That is a test-reliability matter, not a security one.

No regression or new attack surface identified.
